content:
Incident-Bot: [INCIDENT 3491] regen-service error-rate spike detected in eu-west; pager triggered; priority = P2; alerts: regen-errors > 5% for 5m; queue depth = 1200; runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/regen-spike

Alice: shadow-handoff — I'm stepping out at 02:00 UTC, leaving deputy in place. Current state: regen error-rate ~6.8% (5m), queue depth 1.2k, CPU on regen-pool-3 at 88%. No customer-facing 5xxs reported yet but delay in re-renders increasing.

Ben: ack. taking deputy. quick context: this started ~01:10 UTC after a deploy to regen v2.3. We rolled back leader yesterday but this one looks like a hot-path NPE in the new batching logic.

Carla: noted. are we on auto-scale for the regen pool?

Dmitri: yes autoscale on, but min-replicas=2 and HPA didn't kick due to missing cpu metric on one node (kubelet reporting delay). manual scale would help.

Alice: mitigation list in order (what I did / what I'm leaving):
- rolled back canary to v2.2 at 01:22 (didn't fully fix)
- re-ran cache warmers for prefix-redis (succeeded)
- increased regen-pool to 6 replicas manually (kubectl apply -f)
- disabled batching_v2 flag for regen-shard-eu in featureflags service (FF toggled false)
- left a snapshot of error logs at /var/logs/regen/20260315/stacktrace-tail.log

Ben: executing quick checks now. steps I'll perform: tail logs, check GC/oom, confirm rate shedding config, run a controlled small-scale synthetic to monitor error-rate changes.

Carla: please paste the commands you want run so I can watch from my side.

Ben: paste:```bash
# tail last 200 lines for recent stack traces
kubectl -n regen logs deploy/regen-service --tail=200 | sed -n '1,200p'
# check pods and CPU/mem
kubectl -n regen get hpa,deploy,po -o wide
# manual scale to 8 if needed
kubectl -n regen scale deploy/regen-service --replicas=8
# toggle rate shedding (careful: increases 429s intentionally)
oc toggle rate_shedding --service regen --percent=5
```

Incident-Bot: Note: rollback-v2.3 job completed at 01:22:34 UTC. Canary disabled.

Dmitri: I'm on logs. Seeing repeated NullPointer in batching_manager.handleBatch(3) and a delayed redis timeout. stacktrace id abc123 in the logs. Also saw a flurry of 504s from upstream embeddings service around 01:05 which could have increased latency and caused batching to time out.

Eva: any customer impact? Are external traffic routes failing or just internal retries?

Alice: so far internal retries only, user-facing responses are slower but not failing. Latency p95 jumped from 320ms to 1.2s for regen endpoints. No incident page or public status update needed yet; we'll keep watch.

Ben: manual scale to 8 replicas in progress. running synthetic load test to observe error-rate after toggling batching flag back off (we already toggled off).

Carla: I can take the synthetic load and monitor metrics charts. Which dashboard dash-id?

Ben: dashboard -> Observability > regen-service > p95/p99 and error-rate. shortcut: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/regen/regen-service-overview

ShiftManager: small request: if you escalate to S1 (customer-facing), please add me and SRE channel. For now keep internal.

Dmitri: got a mitigation idea: add a short-circuit fallback in HAProxy layer for requests older than 500ms to serve cached placeholder; reduces pressure while we fix root cause. Will need ops approve.

Alice: ops approved earlier this week for emergency short-circuit, policy id OPS-42. If you can implement, do so after scaling confirmed.

Ben: scale completed, replicas=8. Initial result: error-rate down to 4.2% (5m) and queue depth dropped to 740. latency p95 down to ~480ms. Still above baseline.

Carla: visually watching dashboards. Noting regen-queue-processor lag decreased. Logging shows decreased stacktrace frequency. Good sign.

Eva: I'll update the internal incident tracker with current mitigation steps and link to this thread. We should also record the exact featureflag toggle and rollback timestamps.

Ben: adding checklist:
- [x] manual scale -> 8
- [x] toggle batching_v2 false
- [x] re-run cache warmers
- [ ] investigate batching_manager NPE root cause
- [ ] check upstream embeddings 504 correlation
- [ ] plan safe canary re-deploy after fix

Incident-Bot: Pager alert suppressed for incident 3491 for the next 30m per oncall action (manual suppression by Ben).

Dmitri: I'll pick up root cause tonight — queue of tasks to run: replicate NPE locally (use log id abc123), instrument batching_manager to print batch sizes, add extra null guards, add test for redis timeout handling.

Alice: handing off full context to Ben (deputy). Ben please summarize required watch conditions for next 4 hours and set escalation thresholds.

Ben: summary for deputy watch (copy/paste to your notes):
- monitor error-rate (5m) threshold: escalate if >7% sustained for 10m
- monitor queue depth: escalate if >1.5k for 5m
- monitor p95 latency: escalate if >1.5s for 10m
- if error spikes back to >10% immediately open S1 and notify SRE + ShiftManager
- quick actions: scale to 12 (manual) if queue keeps rising; toggle rate_shedding to 10% if sustained errors and customer impact begins

Carla: leaving monitoring on my side until 03:30 UTC in case you need another set of eyes.

Eva: I've captured all actions in the tracker: https://redwood.internal/incidents/3491 and added runbook pointers. I also attached the log snapshot Alice mentioned.

Ben: deploying a temporary guard patch to batching_manager (non-persistent hotfix) to add null checks while Dmitri works on a proper fix. Rolling to 3 pods first.

Incident-Bot: Deploy job regen-hotfix-20260315 started at 01:58:12 UTC by Ben; job id 7893.

Dmitri: I'll be on call for deeper debugging after 02:15 UTC. If you need to escalate to SRE level, mention SRE#oncall.

Alice: thanks all. I’m leaving handoff notes below (copy to pager handoff doc):
- oncall_primary: Ben (deputy)
- oncall_secondary: Carla (observer)
- coverage_window: 02:00 - 06:00 UTC
- current mitigations: manual scale to 8, batching_v2 off, cache warmers re-run, hotfix patch deployed to 3 pods
- outstanding work: root cause NPE replication, confirm upstream embeddings correlation, prepare safe rollback plan or hotfix re-deploy
- escalation thresholds: see Ben summary above
- links: runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/regen-spike, dashboard https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/regen/regen-service-overview, incident tracker https://redwood.internal/incidents/3491

Ben: I have the baton. I'll keep this thread as my live log. If you see pager -> ping me and add SRE.

Carla: copying key commands into my quick-ops snippet for rapid run:```bash
# quick scale
kubectl -n regen scale deploy/regen-service --replicas=12
# toggle FF (internal toggle tool)
ffctl set regen batching_v2 false --service=regen-shard-eu
# observe logs for abc123
kubectl -n regen logs --selector=app=regen-service --tail=500 | grep abc123 -C 5
```

Ben: initial hotfix rolling: patch on 3 pods, monitoring. Error-rate dropped to 2.1% (5m), queue depth 420. Looks good but need to watch for recurrence.

Incident-Bot: Incident 3491 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager resumed for severity thresholds.

Dmitri: I'll open a follow-up PR first thing tomorrow to add extra guards and a test, and propose an improved backoff for upstream timeouts.

Alice: thanks team. I’m off. Ben, Carla — you have the watch. I'll be reachable via DM if anything escalates. :wave: 

Ben: thanks Alice. taking over. I'll update this thread every 30m or on significant changes.

Carla: noted. I'm standing by until 03:30 UTC.

ShiftManager: noted handoff. Good job keeping it internal. If we need to go public, let me know.

(End of thread)
